use_when.text: Use Lost and Found to show what kind of report an item is.
Use Potential Match when a found item may belong to a lost report.
Use Claim Pending until staff review the claim, then switch to Verified or Rejected.
Use Returned once the item is back with its owner.
Put it next to the item name in cards, table rows and the item detail header.

dont_use_when.text: Do not use it as a button or filter. Use Filter Chip for filtering.
Do not change the label to a word that does not match the status.
Do not recolour it outside the status tokens.
Do not show more than one status badge for the same item.
Do not use it for counts or general tags.

best_practice.text: Keep one status per item and update the badge as the item moves through the process.
Turn on Dot only in long lists where it helps people scan. Keep it off everywhere else.

placement.text: Item Card body, above the Title.
Table Row, Body type: the Status column, fifth cell.

a11y.text: Renders a <span> with no role; the label text is the Status value.
Sets no aria-live; announcing status changes is left to the page.
Do not rely on colour alone. The label always names the status.
Mark the dot aria-hidden="true". It is decorative.
When the status changes on screen, announce it with a polite live region (aria-live="polite").
Give the column a header such as Status so screen readers read the badge in context.
Label contrast is above 4.5:1 on every status background.

gaps.detail: Status Badge composes no other component and no story pairs it with a sibling component.
